Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-01T09:12:00Z
Subject: Draft MAP & eval plan for TTFT streaming benchmark

Hi Danielle,

Attached is a first draft of the Mutual Action Plan (tabbed MAP) and the proposed evaluation plan for the time-to-first-token (TTFT) + streaming latency run for chat/text generation. High level: we want a shared acceptance bar and a close timeline that aligns Redwood's Dedicated trial with CareWell's go/no-go decision.

Key proposal (please review):
- Acceptance criteria (initial): p50 <= 120ms, p95 <= 350ms, p99 <= 650ms at 50 concurrent streaming sessions with typical prompt mix (avg input 120 tokens, 512 max)
- Bench configuration: hosted API (r6g-equivalent), model: rw-chat-medium-1 (quantized FP16), auto-batching enabled, warmup 500 tokens, 3 runs for stability
- Timeline: smoke run week of Nov 8, full sweep week of Nov 15 (24h continuous), results report Nov 18, decision/close Nov 22

Action items I put in the MAP spreadsheet (CAREWELL_MAP_v2.xlsx): test prompts, concurrency matrix, trace sample collection, security checkpoint.

Please let me know if you want different acceptance numbers or if you want the run on a dedicated pool instead of hosted API. Happy to adjust.

Thanks,
Olga

Date: 2026-11-08T11:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Draft MAP & eval plan for TTFT streaming benchmark

Olga,

Thanks for the fast turnaround and the MAP. A few clarifying items from our side before we lock the timeline: 

- Concurrency: 50 streams sounds representative, but can you add rows for 10 and 100 as part of the sweep? We need to understand the slope as we scale.
- Prompts: we'll provide 20 production-like prompts; can Redwood confirm whether prompt truncation or tokenization differences are expected to affect TTFT measures?
- Environment: we prefer the Dedicated trial for the final run if possible (to reflect our intended production mode). Is there a way to run the full sweep on a dedicated pool?

Also: security wants an explicit note about data retention of trace files and whether traces include examples of PHI — we will mark those prompts accordingly.

Small ask: can we relax p99 to 700ms if the p95 stays under 350ms? If not, flag and we can discuss tradeoffs.

I'll update the MAP spreadsheet with our procurement and legal timelines on our side. If you can confirm the run plan by Nov 10 we can keep the week-of-Nov-15 window.

Best,
Danielle
Director, Conversational AI
CareWell Health

Date: 2026-11-12T14:22:00Z
Subject: RE: Draft MAP & eval plan for TTFT streaming benchmark

OLGA / LAURA — short note on bench implementation details so Danielle has full context.

Planned bench setup (summary):
- Model: rw-chat-medium-1 (quantized int8 path verified, fallback FP16 for correctness checks)
- HW: Dedicated A100-equivalent nodes for main sweep; host-run for quick smoke runs
- Sequence profile: mean input 120 tokens, output up to 256 tokens; sampling top-p=0.9
- Measurement: client-side TTFT (wall-clock first token received) + server trace (enqueue-to-first-byte), we will provide both metrics.
- Warmup: 1k tokens per model instance, then 3 full sweeps per concurrency point (1, 10, 50, 100).
- Noise mitigation: run-run median across sweeps, remove obvious outlier windows (spikes > 2x median for >30s) and report with annotations.

I attached a trimmed trace bundle (trace_samples.jsonl) with anonymized traces and timestamps for them to review. We're provisioning a dedicated pool for Nov 15-17 for the full sweep; will revert if capacity shifts.

Marcus
Sr. Performance Engineer, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Attachment: trace_samples.jsonl (trace stub)
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>
To: Danielle Morris <danielle.morris@carewell.com>
Cc: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:07:00Z
Subject: Results: TTFT & streaming sweep (summary) + next steps

Danielle / James — thanks for the collab. We completed the dedicated-pool sweep Nov 15-17. Attached is an executive summary (ttft_stream_bench_summary_20261120.pdf) and the raw annotated traces are available on the secure share link in the MAP. Highlights below (all TTFT measured as client-observed time-to-first-token):

Sweep summary (selected rows):
- Concurrency 1: p50 38ms, p95 120ms, p99 250ms
- Concurrency 10: p50 62ms, p95 220ms, p99 420ms
- Concurrency 50: p50 95ms, p95 380ms, p99 720ms
- Concurrency 100: p50 160ms, p95 620ms, p99 980ms

Notes and observations:
- We saw two short stability windows during the 24h run where median latency spiked (~60s each). Traces indicate those correlate with background model cache eviction and one autoscaler event. Those windows are annotated in the PDF.
- p95 meets the 350ms target at lower concurrencies but is slightly above at 50 (measured 380ms). p99 at 50 is 720ms, which is above your relaxed 700ms ask by 20ms.
- Enabling prefix/KV caching reduced p99 at 50 to ~600ms in a targeted follow-up run (we included that mini-sweep as an appendix). That change requires a short config change on your side and a brief canary period.

Proposed next steps (in MAP spreadsheet):
1) Canaries: enable prefix cache + run 12h canary (target Nov 19) — action: Redwood (Marcus)
2) Legal/Procurement: CareWell to send PO or sign-off by Nov 22 to enter Dedicated trial pricing — action: CareWell (Danielle / James)
3) SLA adjustments: if canary confirms p99 <= 650ms we lock acceptance and schedule Dedicated trial onboarding Nov 29 — action: joint

If you accept the canary flow we will kick off the config change tonight and run the 12h test overnight.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference

Attachment: ttft_stream_bench_summary_20261120.pdf (report stub)
